input.understanding: The target is a Go Raft library with leader, follower and candidate roles, externally supplied log/stable/snapshot stores, transport and FSM. The main loop handles protocol and admission work; replication goroutines report progress; an asynchronous FSM goroutine executes application work; snapshots are captured through the FSM and persisted separately. Commitment tracks voter IDs and a leader-start threshold. Optional batching, pre-vote, protocol versions and startup snapshot restoration affect applicability. The supplied evidence supports a bounded commitment-accounting check and a higher-priority inquiry into acknowledgment provenance after truncation and persistence failure.
input.selection_rationale: Rank U_append_error_support first for investigation because its concrete error crossing may invalidate a fact consumed as consensus support. It requires focused evidence before an executable scenario is justified. Rank U_commit_accounting second overall and first for immediate local checking because its implementation is complete and its oracle can be separated from input provenance. Application completion and snapshot recovery are consequential but remain responsibility-level inquiries rather than manufactured checked claims.

Inspect configuration fields and their documented conditions for timeouts, batching, snapshots, startup restoration and election mechanisms. Resolve which behaviors are configurable without assuming defaults or deployment settings.

Inspect NewRaft initialization, persistent-state reads, adapter selection and background-work startup. Identify recovery dependencies and distinguish initialized state from guarantees requiring restoration helpers.

Inspect Apply, ApplyLog, Barrier, VerifyLeader and GetConfiguration contracts and entry points. Resolve what client requests enqueue, what timeout means and which completion or authority claims need downstream evidence.
Inspect follower event handling and timeout transitions. Identify actual triggers, membership filters and request handling before deriving election or authority-maintenance questions.

Inspect configuration-change request fields, configuration history representation, voting eligibility and validation. Resolve how identities and latest versus committed membership are represented; activation timing requires consumer evidence.

Inspect support aggregation, configuration replacement, match updates and commit advancement. Identify the precise inputs and historical constraints the aggregator consumes without assuming those inputs are valid.

Inspect ordinary replication request execution and response handling. Resolve how successful, failed or stale responses affect progress and identify support producers and helper dependencies; pipeline and snapshot paths remain separate.

Sample the leader event loop to locate commit-notification consumption, configuration interactions and outstanding-work handling. This is a partial function read; later event branches remain explicitly unexplored.

Inspect dispatchLogs, processLogs and prepareLog together. Resolve normal-path local persistence ordering, storage-error handling, support publication and the handoff from selected log entries to FSM work and futures.

Inspect AppendEntries acceptance, history comparison, truncation, persistence, commit propagation and configuration-log processing. Identify what a successful response establishes and which prior-context or storage assumptions require further evidence.

Inspect FSM, BatchingFSM and snapshot interface contracts plus the beginning of runFSM. Resolve application filtering, batch-result correlation and visible completion behavior while retaining any truncated helper or event-loop logic as an open dependency.

Inspect snapshot capture-to-persistence coordination and compaction with trailing logs. Resolve which state and configuration accompany a snapshot and what successful operations precede deletion; sink durability and recovery consumption require separate reads.

input.understanding: The target is a Go Raft library with leader, follower and candidate roles, externally supplied log/stable/snapshot stores, transport and FSM. The main loop handles protocol and admission work; replication goroutines report progress; an asynchronous FSM goroutine executes application work; snapshots are captured through the FSM and persisted separately. Commitment tracks voter IDs and a leader-start threshold. Optional batching, pre-vote, protocol versions and startup snapshot restoration affect applicability. The supplied evidence supports a bounded commitment-accounting check and a higher-priority inquiry into acknowledgment provenance after truncation and persistence failure.
input.selection_rationale: Rank U_append_error_support first for investigation because its concrete error crossing may invalidate a fact consumed as consensus support. It requires focused evidence before an executable scenario is justified. Rank U_commit_accounting second overall and first for immediate local checking because its implementation is complete and its oracle can be separated from input provenance. Application completion and snapshot recovery are consequential but remain responsibility-level inquiries rather than manufactured checked claims.
